title: Establish Archivist regression and smoke test harness
goal: Create a durable local regression and smoke test harness for Archivist service contracts, desktop browser behavior, document rendering coverage, and future review/edit workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Define local npm commands for service endpoint smoke, frontend build, desktop browser smoke, and screenshot/evidence capture
Implement the first harness with lightweight local smoke tooling, using Python stdlib scripts plus existing npm commands and headless Chrome instead of introducing Playwright, Cypress, or cloud CI
Cover fast service fixture checks against epp-seed where useful and parity checks against epp-full where real corpus behavior matters

Service smoke verifies /api/status, /api/workspaces, /api/workspaces/epp-full, /api/workspaces/epp-full/navigation, representative document-read endpoints, and absence of SG-0007 staging workspace discovery
Navigation smoke verifies epp-full document completeness and expected library counts for Emergency Preparedness Program, Survey Guidance, and CFR

Document-read smoke verifies rendered compatibility output, stable anchors, sanitized metadata, source/compliance orientation, Appendix A artifact context, and the missing Evacuation Floor Plans fallback payload
Browser smoke captures deterministic desktop screenshots for the default EPP document, Appendix A, Survey Guidance, CFR, and the service-required retry state
Browser smoke uses document-level hash routes and asserts visible markers for selected navigation, selected library, reader title, and Appendix A workbook entry point
Harness writes disposable evidence under .tmp/archivist-smoke or an equivalent ignored local evidence folder and prints a concise command summary
Harness fails clearly when local service, Vite server, Chrome, or expected response contracts are unavailable; it does not silently skip primary coverage
Provide a documented path for expanding into renderer parity samples, workbook flows, proposal/review flows, and history/audit checks as those features land
Document when tests are expected to run locally before handoff and what evidence should be captured
non_goals: Blocking SG-0013 on the full regression harness
Pixel-perfect visual regression for every document
Formal browser test framework adoption in this slice
External tracker sync or cloud-only CI as the first test path
Full renderer parity assertions for every document
Persistent screenshot baselines or visual diff approval workflows
Running imports or mutating workspace content as part of normal smoke tests
validation: Run the documented service smoke command
Run the documented desktop browser smoke command
Run the documented combined local smoke/regression command once the harness exists

technical_defaults.summary: Use lightweight local smoke tooling first instead of adopting a formal browser test framework.
details: Use Python stdlib scripts, existing npm commands, and headless Chrome screenshots.
Defer Playwright, Cypress, cloud CI, and persistent visual baselines until renderer and workbook behavior stabilizes.

technical_defaults.summary: Write smoke evidence to an ignored local evidence directory.
details: Use .tmp/archivist-smoke/<run-id>/ or an equivalent ignored local folder for screenshots and machine-readable summaries.
Print a concise pass/fail summary with command names and evidence paths.

technical_defaults.summary: Smoke scripts may manage temporary local child processes but must not install daemon runners.
details: Scripts may start the Archivist service and Vite app when needed.
Scripts should stop child processes after completion and fail clearly on port conflicts or unavailable local capabilities.

technical_defaults.summary: Use desktop-only headless Chrome smoke at stable viewport sizes.
details: Use a stable desktop viewport such as 1440x1000.
Defer mobile coverage, pixel-perfect regression, and screenshot diff approval workflows.

prep_summary.resolved_human_choice: Use lightweight local smoke tooling for the first harness instead of adopting a formal browser test framework.

changed_surfaces: scripts/smoke_archivist.py adds the lightweight local smoke harness for service and browser coverage
package.json exposes smoke:service, smoke:browser, and smoke:all
docs/implementation/sg-0015-regression-smoke-harness-checklist.md documents the implemented commands, coverage, evidence contract, and future expansion path

validation_commands.evidence: Run service-20260527T032929Z verified status, workspace discovery, epp-full/epp-seed manifests, navigation counts, representative document reads, Appendix A artifact context, and missing Markdown fallback.
Run browser-20260527T033008Z captured default EPP, Appendix A, Survey Guidance, CFR, and service-required screenshots with DOM marker checks.
Run all-20260527T033145Z produced summary.json, service-summary.json, browser-summary.json, and five screenshots under .tmp/archivist-smoke/all-20260527T033145Z.

evidence: Service smoke confirms only epp-full and epp-seed are discoverable; no staging workspace candidate is exposed.
Navigation smoke confirms 261 documents with library counts EPP 177, Survey Guidance 52, and CFR 32.
Document smoke confirms rendered HTML and stable anchors for a policy document, Appendix A, E-0001 Survey Guidance, and 42 CFR 483.73.
Appendix A smoke confirms source/compliance orientation and hva-workbook-v1 artifact context.
Missing-document smoke confirms DOC-EVACUATION-EVACUATION_FLOOR_PLANS remains reachable with a clear missing Markdown fallback payload.
Browser smoke captured screenshots for default EPP, Appendix A, Survey Guidance, CFR, and service-required retry state.
Browser smoke starts and stops temporary service/Vite child processes; ports 8798 and 5173 were free after validation.
residual_risks: DOM assertions are marker-based and intentionally lighter than a formal browser framework.
Screenshots are disposable local evidence under .tmp and are not tracked baselines.
Pixel diffing, mobile coverage, Playwright/Cypress adoption, and persistent visual approvals remain deferred.
Browser smoke requires local headless Chrome and control of port 8798 so it can verify the service-required state; the script fails clearly if that port is already occupied.

notes: Created from prep agreement that SG-0013 should have repeatable desktop smoke, while broader regression coverage should live as its own future quality-infrastructure slice rather than bloating the browser-shell build. On 2026-05-27 the first harness style was resolved as lightweight local smoke tooling: Python stdlib scripts plus existing npm commands and headless Chrome, with formal browser frameworks deferred until behavior stabilizes.
